about.title: Turning emerging tech into systems that survive reality
about.lead: Merijn Kersten is an XR engineer and systems builder with 9+ years creating AR, VR and multiplayer applications — across government, healthcare, energy, education and entertainment.
body: He builds systems rather than isolated features, combining software engineering, UX, backend infrastructure, 3D content, hardware and organisational workflows. His technical background spans Unity, Unreal Engine, networking, cloud services, web, AI, computer vision, geospatial technologies and interactive installations.

His projects range from hyper-casual mobile games and educational AR books to medical visualisation, utility infrastructure and training simulators for the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee — including HoloLens solutions using RTK GPS for centimetre-accurate placement of transformers, digital-twin tools built on point clouds and geo-data, and AI-driven conversational characters.

He works with technologies before they mature — ARKit and ARCore before AR Foundation, multiplayer AR, Visual Positioning Systems, Vision Pro, computer vision and generative AI. Unreliable networks, hardware limits, organisational resistance and imperfect tracking taught him to design around real constraints rather than ideal conditions.
In essence, he takes emerging technologies and turns them into robust systems that survive contact with reality — most comfortable in uncertain environments where requirements are still evolving.
